h1: The 6 Best Utility Carts of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 rolling utility carts for garage, shop and kitchen, scored on load rating, shelf depth, wheel brakes and frame material.
summary: The YITAHOME 2-tier plastic cart is the best utility cart: a 550 lb rating, locking brakes and a 45 by 25 inch footprint. MaxWorks owns the heavy-duty middle with two 500 lb carts, while its 3-shelf 80774 is the lighter 225 lb option. The YASONIC metal cart suits a kitchen or craft room, and SUNALLY adds a drawer for small items at the lowest price.
intro: A utility cart's load rating is the number every listing leads with, and it is the least useful one. A cart rated for 500 lb on a perfectly flat shop floor still tips if you park it on a slope with the heaviest box on the top shelf. Wheel brakes, shelf depth and frame stiffness decide whether that rating means anything in your garage.

We reviewed six rolling carts from their listed specs, comparing capacity, shelf count, brakes, material and footprint. Four are polypropylene service carts built for shops and garages, one is a metal frame cart and one is a light three-tier model with a drawer. Rankings reward carts that publish their numbers, because several listings do not.

products.name: YITAHOME 2 Tier Heavy Duty Plastic Utility Cart 45 x 25 Inch
products.verdict: The highest stated capacity here at 550 lb, with locking brakes on a 45 by 25 inch deck.
products.description:
The YITAHOME is a two-tier cart made of polypropylene with a stated 550 lb capacity, locking brakes and a 45 x 25 inch footprint.

Brakes are what move it ahead of the MaxWorks 500 lb carts. A cart that rolls while you load a heavy box is the common failure, and locking wheels prevent it. The extra 50 lb of rating is a bonus rather than the reason.

Buy it for a garage, workshop or loading area. The caveat is the price, a tier above the lightest plastic carts, and the listing does not state shelf height or wheel diameter.
products.idealFor: Garages and workshops moving heavy boxes.
products.skipIf: You need a narrow cart for tight aisles.

products.name: MaxWorks 2‐Tier Heavy‐Duty Utility Service Cart 500 lb Capacity 46" x 25.5" x
products.verdict: Three-inch deep shelves with side rails and a 500 lb rating at 46 x 25.5 inches.
products.description:
This MaxWorks cart has a 500 lb capacity, lightweight polypropylene that resists rust, and spacious shelves 3 inches deep with integrated side rails. It measures 46 x 25.5 inches.

The raised side rails are the reason it ranks above the plain 2-shelf MaxWorks: items stay on the shelf when you turn a corner. It trails the YITAHOME on rating by 50 lb and on brake detail, since the listing names none.

It suits shops and garages. The caveat is that brakes are not described, so check before using it on a slope.
products.idealFor: Shops needing rails to keep tools in place.

products.name: MaxWorks Heavy Duty 2‐Shelf Service Cart 500 lb Capacity Polypropylene Utility
products.verdict: A 500 lb polypropylene service cart with easy assembly at a lower price tier.
products.description:
The MaxWorks 2-shelf cart is rated 500 lb, is made of polypropylene and is described as easy to maintain and assemble.

It is the same capacity as the 2-tier MaxWorks, but the listing offers fewer details, so it ranks below it. Its edge is price, one tier lower, for the same rated load.

Choose it if you want heavy-duty capacity without paying for extras. Expect to measure your aisle yourself, because the thin spec list gives no dimensions, brakes or shelf depth, and plan to add rubber stops if your floor slopes toward a drain.
products.idealFor: Budget-conscious shops needing a high rating.
products.skipIf: You need to see full dimensions first.

products.name: MaxWorks 80774 3-Shelf Utility Plastic Cart with Wheels-225 Lbs Maximum Capacity
products.verdict: Three injection-molded shelves on aluminum legs, rated 225 lb.
products.description:
The 80774 has three shelves of injection-molded polypropylene on aluminum legs, with a 225 lb maximum capacity.

Three shelves give more separation for supplies than the 2-tier carts, and aluminum legs will not rust. It ranks fourth because 225 lb is less than half the rating of the heavy-duty MaxWorks carts.

It fits kitchens, craft rooms and light shop duty. Its limit is the lower rating, so it is not the cart for a case of tools or a stack of paint cans. Keep the heaviest items on the bottom shelf and the aluminum legs will stay straight for years of kitchen and craft work.
products.idealFor: Light-duty supplies in kitchens and craft rooms.

products.name: YASONIC 3 Tier Metal Rolling Cart
products.verdict: A coated metal three-tier cart with patent-pending frame geometry for moving under load.
products.description:
The YASONIC is a three-tier metal rolling cart with patent-pending frame geometry meant to spread weight, a durable coating and wheels the maker says move easily under heavy loads.

A metal frame looks better in a kitchen or office than plastic. It ranks fifth because the listing states no capacity, so you cannot compare it with the rated carts above.

Choose it for display and light storage. The caveat is that the missing load rating means you should treat it as a light cart.
products.skipIf: You need a stated load rating.

products.name: SUNALLY 3 Tier Rolling Cart with Drawer
products.verdict: A three-tier cart with a drawer, brake wheels and tool-free assembly.
products.description:
The SUNALLY has three tiers and a drawer for small items, smooth-glide wheels with brakes and a tool-free assembly.

The drawer is what sets it apart, since loose items such as screws and craft supplies stay out of sight. It ranks last because no capacity or dimensions are given, and the price tier is the lowest.

It works for craft, beauty and bathroom storage. It sits below the metal YASONIC on looks and above nothing on strength, so treat it as a light-duty cart, not a service cart, and keep the drawer for lightweight items so the slides last.
products.skipIf: You need to carry heavy items.

whatMatters.detail: The stated capacity is the maximum weight the cart is rated to hold, spread evenly. Heavy loads on one shelf or one corner are harder on it. Choose a rating well above your heaviest load, and be careful with listings that give no number, since they are usually light-duty.

A loaded cart rolls away if one wheel is free during loading. Locking brakes on two or more wheels stop that, which matters in garages and on loading ramps. Look for the word brakes or locking on the listing, and treat the absence as a warning on sloped floors.

Shelves with raised side rails keep items from sliding off when you turn. A 3 inch deep shelf also holds bins and cans more securely than a flat panel. Read the shelf description for rails or lips, and choose them if the cart travels over thresholds.

Polypropylene will not rust and wipes clean, aluminum legs add stiffness without rust, and coated steel is strong but can chip. Match the material to the room: plastic suits wet garages, while a coated metal cart suits a kitchen or office.

A 45 or 46 inch long cart carries more but needs wide aisles and a wide door. Measure your narrowest turn before you buy. Listings that publish length and width, like the YITAHOME and MaxWorks 2-tier, make this easy, while others leave you guessing.

faq.q: Will a plastic cart hold 500 lb?
faq.a: The MaxWorks carts and YITAHOME are rated for 500 to 550 lb of evenly spread load on polypropylene. Keep heavy items low and centered. The MaxWorks 80774 is rated for only 225 lb, so do not treat them alike.

faq.q: What mistake do buyers make with utility carts?
faq.a: Trusting the load rating alone. A cart with no brakes can roll while you load it. The YITAHOME lists locking brakes, so it is safer on a slope than carts that stay silent about wheels.

faq.q: Is the 2-tier MaxWorks worth it over the 2-shelf?
faq.a: If shelf rails matter, yes. Both are rated 500 lb, but the 2-tier adds 3 inch deep shelves with side rails and lists 46 x 25.5 inches. The 2-shelf costs a tier less.
The MaxWorks 2-shelf and SUNALLY describe easy or tool-free assembly, and the MaxWorks 80774 has aluminum legs that are easy to install. Expect to need a second pair of hands for the 46 inch carts.

faq.q: How do I clean a polypropylene cart?
faq.a: Wipe with soapy water and rinse. Polypropylene shrugs off oil and moisture, which is why the MaxWorks and YITAHOME suit garages. Avoid harsh solvents, which can cloud the plastic.

faq.q: Can I use a metal cart outside?
faq.a: Not for long. The YASONIC has a coating, but metal frames can rust if the finish chips. For outdoor or wet use, a rust-resistant plastic cart such as the YITAHOME is the safer choice.

finalTake: The YITAHOME 2-tier is the best utility cart because it combines the highest rating, locking brakes and a generous deck. The MaxWorks 2-tier is the better shelf design, and the 2-shelf MaxWorks is the cheaper heavy-duty route. Choose the SUNALLY or YASONIC only for light storage, since neither states a load rating.
